scope: Proposition 4.2 (Small labeled integral vectors) of the manuscript “Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold” (preprints/Quaternionic-Division-Points-on-Curves-in-the-Siegel-Threefold-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e11b4b068502ced9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are constants c, C > 0 with the following property. For every target t, an extension L/K(t) of degree at most C defines all geometric endomorphisms of At. There are two independent endomorphisms u1, u2 ∈ EndL(At) which are symmetric and trace free, span Et, and satisfy qλt (uj) ≤ C(dh)c (j = 1, 2). (4.1) The corresponding labeled vectors are denoted P = (P1, P2) in de Rham coordinates. Con- jugating a labeled target always means conjugating these endomorphisms as well. This pair need not generate the saturated integral cohomology lattice of Et.
